name: Chemical Kinetics
tagline: Reaction rates, mechanisms, and transition-state theory.

definition.lead: Chemical kinetics measures how fast reactions go and uncovers the step-by-step path they follow.
definition.body: Thermodynamics says whether a reaction can happen; kinetics says whether it happens in a second or in a million years. Rate laws, activation energies and mechanisms let chemists speed up the reactions they want and slow down the ones they don't, from drug degradation to engine combustion.

facts.label: rule of thumb: many reaction rates roughly double for every 10 °C rise
Arrhenius links reaction rate to temperature
a femtosecond: the timescale on which bonds break

timeline.title: The first measured rate
timeline.text: Ludwig Wilhelmy follows the conversion of sucrose over time.
timeline.why: The first quantitative study of reaction speed.

timeline.title: The law of mass action
timeline.text: Cato Guldberg and Peter Waage relate rates and equilibrium to concentrations.
timeline.why: The ancestor of every rate law.

timeline.title: Études de dynamique chimique
timeline.text: Van 't Hoff publishes his book on chemical dynamics and reaction order.
timeline.why: Laid out kinetics as a quantitative science.

timeline.title: The Arrhenius equation
timeline.text: Svante Arrhenius introduces the activation energy.
timeline.why: Explained why temperature matters so much.

timeline.title: Enzyme kinetics
timeline.text: Leonor Michaelis and Maud Menten publish their model of enzyme rates.
timeline.why: Still the first model taught for every enzyme.

timeline.title: Transition state theory
timeline.text: Henry Eyring, and independently Evans and Polanyi, describe the activated complex.

timeline.title: Chain reactions
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Nikolay Semenov and Cyril Hinshelwood for the mechanisms of chemical reactions.

timeline.title: Fast reactions
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Eigen, Norrish and Porter for studying extremely fast reactions.

timeline.title: Reaction dynamics
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Herschbach, Lee and Polanyi for the dynamics of elementary reactions.
timeline.why: Single collisions between molecules, studied one by one.

timeline.title: Femtochemistry
timeline.why: The transition state itself became observable.

quiz.q: For a first-order reaction, the half-life…
options: Does not depend on the starting concentration
quiz.explain: t½ = ln 2 / k: always the same time to halve, whatever the amount.

quiz.q: What are the units of a first-order rate constant?
If rate = k[A]², doubling [A] makes the rate…

options: The slowest step of the mechanism
quiz.explain: Like the narrowest point of a funnel, it limits the overall rate.

options: The barrier between reactants and the transition state
The bond energy of the product
quiz.explain: Only molecules with at least this energy can react.

quiz.q: A catalyst speeds up a reaction by…
quiz.explain: It lowers the barrier and is regenerated at the end.

options: The substrate concentration at half the maximum rate
The maximum rate the enzyme can reach
The total enzyme concentration in the assay
The amount of product formed per minute
quiz.explain: A low Km means the enzyme works well even at low substrate levels.

quiz.q: Why does refrigeration slow food spoilage?
options: Fewer molecules have enough energy to cross the activation barrier
quiz.explain: Rates fall steeply as temperature drops (Arrhenius).

quiz.q: Who first measured a reaction rate quantitatively, in 1850?
quiz.explain: He followed sucrose inversion using the rotation of polarized light.

quiz.q: What are the three stages of a chain reaction?
quiz.explain: Radicals are created, keep regenerating each other, then are destroyed.

quiz.q: On an Arrhenius plot of ln k against 1/T, the slope equals…
quiz.explain: A steeper slope means a higher activation energy.

quiz.q: How does a reaction intermediate differ from a transition state?
options: An intermediate sits in an energy minimum and can sometimes be detected
An intermediate is higher in energy
An intermediate is the final product
quiz.explain: A transition state is an energy maximum that lasts only about one molecular vibration.
